title: High-Performance Unlogged Tables vs Temp Tables for Ephemeral Staging
realWorldScenario: A nightly ETL pipeline loads 20 million raw records from S3, parses and transforms them, and aggregates summary statistics. Using standard tables takes 25 minutes due to massive WAL disk I/O. Using `CREATE TEMP TABLE` causes connection bloat.
questionStatement: Compare PostgreSQL `UNLOGGED` tables with Temporary tables (`TEMP TABLE`) and Standard logged tables. How do unlogged tables bypass the Write-Ahead Log (WAL)? What happens to unlogged tables during a server crash or on a streaming read-replica?
expectedConcepts: Bypassing Write-Ahead Logging for maximum write speed
Automatic truncation to empty table upon crash recovery restart
Cluster-wide visibility vs session-scoped TEMP tables
hints: Why are unlogged tables 5x faster on bulk inserts?
What happens to data in an unlogged table if someone pulls the server power plug?
Do unlogged tables exist on read replicas?
